ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (Article 4 on beneficial ownership identification), as amended; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010); Real Decreto-ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril (Registro de Titularidades Reales connectivity and DAC 6 transposition); Ley 11/2021, de 9 de julio (anti-fraud measures affecting AML evidentiary rules). The UBO register is operated by the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública through the Colegio de Registradores portal.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's country of incorporation (e.g., Companies House, Registro Mercantil, Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization where the origin state is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney executed by the founding shareholders in favor of the incorporating agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction of execution, legalized by the competent ministry and apostilled
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague signatories)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of valid national passports or identity documents of all UBOs and appointed directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/identity issuing authority of each UBO, with notarial certification of the copies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization where applicable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Declaration (for filing to the Registro de Titularidades Reales)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish notary (Notaría) through the Colegio de Registradores electronic platform
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal notarial protocol; no Apostille required as a domestic Spanish instrument

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Tax Residence of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the shareholder's state of residence (e.g., IRS, HMRC, CNBV counterpart)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague signatories)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory positive identification and screening of each UBO, director, and authorized signatory at application intake and again within 48 hours before execution of the notarial deed against: (i) SEPBLAC national financial intelligence measures; (ii) OFAC SDN List; (iii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list; and (v) Bank of Spain public warnings and institutional sanction notices. A positive PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds documentation, and committee-level approval prior to deed execution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) - online denominación social application and negative certificate service at https://www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in Spanish (Castilian) using Latin script under Spanish orthographic norms; co-official languages (Catalan, Basque, Galician) are admissible only where the registered office is situated in a bilingual autonomous community and the Spanish denomination remains consistent. Foreign words may be transliterated only where grammatically acceptable and not confusingly similar to existing denominations. The name must include 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.' and comply with Articles 401-411 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Royal Decree 1784/1996).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms referencing the State or public entities ('España', 'Ministerio', 'Gobierno', 'Ayuntamiento', 'Banco de España') requiring prior ministerial authorization
Royal patronage terms or honorifics ('Real') requiring prior authorization of the Ministry of the Presidency
Financial, insurance, reinsurance, or payment-institution terms ('Banco', 'Caja', 'Seguros', 'Reaseguro') requiring prior authorization of Banco de España or DGSFP
Regulated public-law activity terms ('Fundación', 'Mutualidad', 'Sociedad de Inversión', 'Cooperativa') absent the corresponding supervisory licence
Denominations contrary to law, public order, or morality, or deceptive as to the corporate purpose (including unlicensed claims of pharmaceutical or aseptic certification)
Identical, phonetically equivalent, or confusingly similar names to pre-existing Spanish or EU-registered companies (Article 408 RRM)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No formal extension exists; the certificación negativa de denominación is valid for three months from issuance, after which a new application must be filed in the same priority queue. Upon rejection, counsel must verify the cause and may file up to three fallback denominations in rank order. Where the rejection is based on an erroneous application of Articles 401-411 RRM, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of notification, or a contentious-administrative appeal before the Audiencia Nacional within two months, attaching the Registry denial certificate, the proposed denomination, and comparative registry evidence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual/mail-forwarding office is tolerated only for correspondence and initial formalities; the statutory seat must be a real place where management, the main establishment, or the operative base is located (Article 9 of Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, Ley de Sociedades de Capital). For this export-manufacturing entity, the domicile must be supplemented by physical management and warehouse/technical infrastructure to prevent recharacterization and tax-residence disputes under Article 8 LSC and OECD substance expectations. Virtual office providers must be registered with the Registro Mercantil for address-clearing purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 10-15% within the first 36 months for a standard low-risk export vehicle, rising to 25-35% if the registered office is a mail-only virtual address, if the vehicle has no local payroll or fixed-asset entries, or if high-value capital equipment is invoiced to group entities abroad. AEAT may conduct unannounced inspection visits, and SEPBLAC retains site-inspection powers under Ley 10/2010.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative denomination certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Order JUS/299/2018, electronic procedure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial incorporation deed (escritura pública de constitución) including notarial UBO declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish notary (Notaría) in the seat of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard SL deed; notarial arancel regulated by Royal Decree 1426/1989

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) processing and compliance package for two foreign directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de la Policía (Comisaría de Extranjería) and/or Spanish consular post of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular statutory fees plus certified translation charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostilles, consular legalization, and sworn translations (SWOT) of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Ministry of Justice, foreign ministries, and sworn translators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 40-90 per apostille and EUR 70-150 per sworn translation page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry inscription of the deed of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil provincial (territorial jurisdiction of the registered office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory arancel fixed by Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional and definitive NIF (Tax Identification Code) coordination with AEAT
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; gestoría handling at prevailing market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registro de Titularidades Reales filing and PEP/OFAC/UN/EU consolidated sanctions screening report

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), arts. 1-18, 20-31, 72-89; Código de Comercio (Real Decreto de 22 de agosto de 1885); Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil); Ley 14/2013 de apoyo a los emprendedores (procedimiento 'empresa en un día' por CIRCE/PAE); Ley 21/2013 de evaluación ambiental.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (denominación social) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office (inscripción), coordinated through the Punto de Atención al Emprendedor (PAE) and CIRCE platform; Registradores de España under the Ministerio de Justicia.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de constitución (public deed of incorporation executed before a Spanish Notario) followed by mandatory inscription in the Registro Mercantil Provincial.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, the statutory minimum share capital is EUR 3,000 under art. 4 LSC, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in kind at the execution of the deed; for cash contributions the notary must be provided with a bank deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) issued by a Spanish credit entity with the capital blocked until registration, or alternatively a notarial deposit certificate; the shares (participaciones) must be 100% paid in and no escrow account is legally required beyond this blocked deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the organizational meeting of [Company Name], S.L., the founding shareholders unanimously resolve as follows: (1) the share capital of EUR 3,000 is divided into 3,000 fully subscribed participations of EUR 1.00 each, and has been fully paid up by bank deposit as required under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital; (2) the registered office is adopted at [Address], Madrid, Spain; (3) the corporate object covers the manufacture, assembly, installation and export of high-speed aseptic beverage-bottling lines; (4) [Full Name] is appointed sole administrator with the powers conferred by article 63 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital; and (5) the administrator is authorized to execute the deed, obtain the tax identification number and complete all registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — Ministerio de Justicia, via the CIRCE portal / PAE or by notarial telematic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official application for a negative name certificate through CIRCE/PAE or directly to the RMC, listing up to five proposed corporate names in priority order and stating the corporate object. The RMC issues the certificación negativa de denominación social confirming that the name is not already registered; the certificate is valid for six months, renewable for a further six months. The name reservation must remain valid at deed execution.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form (RMC/CIRCE standard form)
Copy of DNI/NIE/passport of each founding shareholder or the legal representative
List of up to five proposed corporate names in priority order
Brief description of the corporate object for name-similarity assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected for identity or similarity with an existing registered name, refile promptly with the remaining proposed alternatives; the RMC will certify the first available option. The negative certificate may also be renewed, and the notary verifies its validity term immediately before execution of the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Provisional Bank Account and Full Payment of the Statutory Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish credit institution (bank/caja) or the notary's official deposit facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company 'in formation' (sociedad en constitución) at a Spanish bank. Deposit the minimum legal capital of EUR 3,000 in cash (or in kind for an SL with the appropriate valuation and report). Obtain the bank's deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) evidencing the holder, the amount, and the blocked nature of the funds until the deed is registered. If the bank declines, pay the capital directly into the notary's deposit account and obtain the statutory notarial deposit certificate (certificado del Notario de depósito).
required_dossiers: DNI/NIE/passport copies of the shareholders and beneficial owners
Private incorporation contract or draft deed for KYC/AML verification
Appropriation declaration for the account of the company under formation
Beneficial-ownership and AML self-declaration forms
Bank confirmation of the EUR 3,000 capital transfer or deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the certificate or delays due to internal AML checks, use the notarial alternative: deliver the capital value to the notary, who issues the compulsory deposit certificate satisfying the legal requirement; the deposit remains blocked and is released only against the registered deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario (Notary Public) in the territorial district of the registered office, integrated with the Registro Mercantil system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At a scheduled notarial appointment, execute the single public deed of incorporation containing the bylaws (estatutos sociales), corporate object, registered office, capital structure, and administration regime. Each shareholder subscribes and pays in the capital; the notary verifies the negative name certificate, the bank or notarial deposit certificate, and the identity and legal capacity of all parties. The notary certifies the establishment of the SL and issues the first authorized copy (primera copia) for the Mercantile Registry; the deed is subject to the Impuesto de Actos Jurídicos Documentados (IAJD).
required_dossiers: Valid certificación negativa de denominación social
Bank deposit certificate or notarial deposit certificate
Draft corporate bylaws agreed by the shareholders
DNI/NIE/passport of all shareholders and the appointed administrator, with acceptance of office
Documents evidencing representation powers, if any shareholder acts by attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects a defect (expired name certificate, unproven capital payment, or irregular object), cure by replacing the deficient underlying document or by executing a corrective addendum; the deed will not be authorized until the name certificate is valid and the capital contribution is duly evidenced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office — Registradores de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the deed date, deliver the first authorized copy of the deed to the provincial Mercantile Registry together with the regulated registry fee. The registrar verifies compliance with the LSC and the bylaws; once favorably qualified, the company acquires full legal personality and the bank releases the blocked capital upon presentation of an authenticated copy of the inscribed deed. The registry entry is published electronically and the inscription certificate (certificación registral) is later required for the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: Primera copia (authenticated first copy) of the notarial deed
Certificación negativa de denominación social
Bank deposit certificate or notarial deposit certificate
Provisional NIF notice, if already applied (Modelo 036)
Proof of payment of the registry fee (arancel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues an adverse qualification (calificación desfavorable), the notary and shareholders must amend the deed or supply the missing documents within the legal deadline; alternatively, an appeal (expediente gubernativo) may be filed with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration — Provisional and Definitive NIF (Censo de la AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Delegación/Administración corresponding to the tax domicile; for 'empresa en un día' filings via CIRCE/PAE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After deed execution, request the provisional tax identification number (NIF provisional) through CIRCE or by filing Modelo 036 at the competent AEAT office; the provisional NIF is used for the registry filing. Once the Mercantile Registry inscription is obtained, return to AEAT with the registry certificate (certificación registral) to obtain the definitive NIF and complete the start-up census declaration. File Modelo 036/030 as appropriate for tax domicile and obligations.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 (declaración censal) or CIRCE-generated tax forms
Authenticated copy of the deed of incorporation
Certificación registral (inscription certificate of the Mercantile Registry)
Identity documents of the legal representative
Proof of tax domicile (lease contract, property title, or occupancy license)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT returns the filing for discrepancies in the legal representative, domicile, or corporate name, correct the data and resubmit online or at the assigned tax office; ensure the application is lodged with the AEAT administration in the district of the tax domicile to avoid referrals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Activity License and Start-of-Activity Filing (Licencia de Actividad / Declaración Responsable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento (Concejalía de Urbanismo y Medio Ambiente) of the municipality; regional industrial services of the Comunidad Autónoma de Madrid (Dirección General de Industria) for industrial establishment registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing industrial operations in the assembly and packaging-line manufacturing workshop, submit the technical activity project (proyecto de actividad) signed by a competent technician, including acoustics report, fire protection project, and environmental classification documentation. For classified activities, obtain the municipal license or, where permitted, serve the declaración responsable/comunicación previa for start of activity. If the activity triggers a simplified environmental impact assessment under Ley 21/2013, obtain the favorable environmental resolution first. Register the establishment in the industrial registry (RD 697/1995) as required.
required_dossiers: Escritura de constitución and definitive NIF
Technical/industrial activity project with planimetry and description of machinery (ISIC 2825 / NACE 28.29)
Acoustic impact assessment under Ley 37/2003 and municipal ordnance
Fire protection project and compliance declaration under RD 2267/2004
Environmental classification report or simplified EIA documentation, if applicable
Proof of payment of municipal license fees (tasas de actividad)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires corrective technical measures, additional environmental documentation, or a favorable environmental resolution, amend and resubmit the technical project and pay the reassessed municipal fees. An unfavorable license decision may be appealed by lodging a recurso de reposición with the Alcaldía and subsequently before the Juzgado de lo Contencioso-Administrativo.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Industria of the Consejería de Economía (Comunidad de Madrid or corresponding Autonomous Community) in coordination with the municipal Ayuntamiento; national coordination through the Registro Integrado Industrial of the Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo and the Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental of the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Actividad Clasificada / Declaración Responsable de Inicio de Actividad (municipal); Inscripción de Establecimiento Industrial en el Registro Integrado Industrial (RD 697/1995); Declaración CE de Conformidad of the manufactured machinery under the Machinery Directive per RD 1644/2008; workplace opening verification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico — MITERD) and the regional environmental body of the Autonomous Community (Dirección General de Sostenibilidad y Control Ambiental).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C — Environmental Communication (comunicación ambiental) at municipal level for a standard assembly plant; rating rises to 'Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Simplificada' (simplified EIA) only if an Annex II threshold of Ley 21/2013 is exceeded, e.g. plant over 10,000 m² or large metal-fabrication processes. No full EIA or Autorización Ambiental Integrada (AAI/IPPC) is triggered for the assembly of aseptic beverage bottling lines below industrial-emissions thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to public sewer per municipal bylaw: pH 6-9, COD ≤ 500 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L (or stricter local ordinance limits); VOC/air emissions below the thresholds of RD 100/2011 and Directive 2010/75/EU where surface coating/painting operations are present; noise not exceeding 60 dB(A) daytime and 55 dB(A) night at the property boundary under Ley 37/2003; packaging waste and production waste handled pursuant to Ley 7/2022; finished machinery must meet the ISO/EN 415-series and CE-marking safety standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificado de protección contra incendios) and compliance with RD 2267/2004 for industrial establishments; structural load inspection certified by the drafting architect; workplace conditions per RD 486/1997; occupational risk prevention plan per Ley 31/1995 administered by an external prevention service (Servicio de Prevención Ajeno); conformity of electrical installations under RD 842/2002 and work equipment under RD 1215/1997; final opening verification by municipal technical inspectors.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — official online portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity without a permanent establishment in Spain that undertakes economic activities (including exports of machinery) must obtain a Spanish Tax Identification Number (NIF) for non-residents. Procedure: (1) appoint a tax representative resident in Spain (obligatory where the taxpayer is resident in a tax haven, otherwise generally recommended or required in practice for administrative dealings); (2) submit Form 030 (Censo de Obligados Tributarios) or the applicable registry form to AEAT, either electronically via the AEAT portal using an electronic certificate, or through the relevant tax office (Delegación de AEAT); (3) provide certified company incorporation documents, proof of foreign tax residence, and identification of the beneficial owner in accordance with AML obligations; (4) obtain the provisional NIF and register in the Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Withholders (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores); (5) if a fixed or permanent establishment is established, register the permanent establishment (Form 036/037) and obtain a definitive NIF; (6) for VAT purposes, any entity making taxable supplies of goods or services in Spain must register for Spanish VAT (NIF-IVA), and if the entity is established outside the EU (or outside Spain but within the EU, depending on regime), may need to register via Form 036 and, where applicable, appoint a VAT fiscal representative under article 164.Dos of the Spanish VAT Law if not established in the EU or in a State with a reciprocal agreement. A foreign exporting manufacturer that merely sells goods to Spanish customers with title and risk passing outside Spain will generally not need Spanish VAT registration solely because of export sales, but registration is required if it performs domestic taxable transactions (e.g., warranty services in Spain, storage of goods leading to distance sales) or exceeds the distance sales threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a check-the-box classification regime comparable to the US. A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is a corporate entity that is per se subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at entity level. No check-the-box election is available for Spanish domestic entities. However, hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD, incorporated via Law 4/2019 and Royal Decree 3/2020) apply to neutralise mismatches arising from divergent tax classification of the entity or its instruments in another jurisdiction; taxpayers may in certain cross-border scenarios make elections under the Spanish CFC rules, tax transparency rules (e.g., Spanish Fiscal Transparency Regime for certain entities), or under the Spanish general anti-abuse rules, but these are not entity classification elections. Foreign entities may obtain a Spanish NIF and be classified for Spanish tax purposes under their foreign legal form; Spanish law generally respects the tax classification of the foreign entity under its domestic law, subject to substance-over-form and the Treaty/BEPS rules, and no 'treaty election' exists. The entity may elect to apply the Spanish reduced corporate income tax rate for newly created SMEs (25% or reduced 15% for qualifying new entities in their first two years in certain cases, subject to conditions, but this is not an entity classification election). For VAT grouping, the special VAT group regime (Régimen Especial de Grupo de Entidades) is an elective mechanism for entities established in Spain, under article 163 sexies of the Spanish VAT Law, allowing tax consolidation for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.alternative_internal_elective_note: No 'check-the-box' equivalent exists under Spanish law; entity classification of an SL is mandatory as a corporate taxpayer. The only statutory elections relevant to tax classification are (a) the VAT group regime, (b) the option to apply customs/warehousing regimes, and (c) possible elections under the Spanish tax treaty network for treatment as a resident or permanent establishment, none of which are entity classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), governed by the Spanish VAT Law (Ley 37/1992, de 28 de diciembre, del Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) and Royal Decree 1624/1992 implementing regulations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 (no general VAT registration threshold for suppliers established outside Spain; any taxable person who carries out taxable transactions in the Spanish territory is required to register. For intra-EU distance sales of goods to consumers, the distance sales threshold for EU established sellers is EUR 10,000 for sales to final consumers in Spain; for non-established sellers, registration is required immediately upon the first distance sale. For non-established suppliers of B2B services under the reverse charge, no VAT registration is required solely for that supply, but the customer self-assesses. Registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction in Spain; there is no general economic turnover threshold below which a non-resident supplier is exempt from registration.)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates a phased Transition to Real-Time Electronic Invoicing under Law 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece) which obliges all entrepreneurs and professionals to issue electronic invoices in a structured interoperable format, effective from 2025 for large enterprises (turnover > €8 million) and 2026 for all others (deadlines may be technically extended). Additionally, Veri*Factu (Royal Decree 1007/2023 and Order HAC/1177/2023) requires detailed invoice records to be lodged with AEAT through a certified system (software or platform) in a standardised JSON/XML format using a secure QR (QR verifactu) for the invoice signatures and hash chain; for B2B and B2C. The Spanish Tax Agency's Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA (SII) is mandatory for large enterprises and VAT groups (turnover > €6 million or VAT group registration), requiring each invoice to be transmitted electronically to AEAT within 4 calendar days from issuance (8 days for certain periods, proposed 4 days currently applied). For a foreign exporter selling machinery to Spanish businesses with no Spanish establishment and not registered for VAT, SII is not directly applicable; however, if VAT registration exists (e.g., for domestic warranty services or a permanent establishment), compliance with e-invoicing and real-time reporting may be required depending on turnover/status. AEAT requires advance electronic submission of customs export declarations via the CEX/DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) and the ECS (Export Control System); no 'digital stamping' of the invoice is required, but every invoice must be transmitted to the Veri*Factu solution before the issuance and include the QR code; for sales to non-VAT-registered persons the system also applies. Non-resident exporters may need to obtain a Spanish electronic certificate or use an authorised representative to file the SII and Veri*Factu files.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.nexus_specific_rules_for_export_of_goods: For the sale of aseptic beverage bottling lines (machinery) by a Spanish SL to a customer in a foreign country (outside the EU) or to another EU member state, Spanish VAT is generally not charged if the goods are transported out of Spain by the seller, by the customer, or for their account. The supply is subject to zero rating (export) or intra-Community supply exemption, as applicable. If the machinery is installed and tested at a customer site within Spain, that installation supply is taxable in Spain (unless it forms part of an export contract and conditions of exemption are met). The place of supply for the sale of goods without transport is where the goods are located at the time of supply; with transport, where the transport begins. If the goods are exported by a customer (non-resident), the Spanish supplier must obtain and retain proof of export and, for intra-EU, a valid Spanish VAT number of the customer, declarations, and transport documents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.reverse_charge_applicability: For a non-Spanish supplier of machinery into Spain from outside Spain (import/export scenario outside the scope), reverse charge is not the standard for goods physically delivered in Spain. For B2B services (e.g., design/engineering services supplied cross-border to Spanish customer), the place of supply is the customer's territory and the service is subject to Spanish VAT with the customer applying reverse charge (no registration needed for the non-resident supplier unless the customer is not a taxable person or lacks a Spanish VAT ID). A foreign supplier of goods with installation in Spain may be required to register for Spanish VAT or, for intra-EU B2B transactions, the place of supply is the customer's territory with reverse charge only for intra-Community acquisitions and certain services, not for supplies with installation. For aseptic bottling line exports: if the goods are exported outside the EU and the Spanish SL is the exporter, the zero rate applies with supporting export documentation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.commercial_warranty_and_after_sales_serv: If the Spanish SL provides after-sales warranty services in Spain (e.g., employees sent to Spain or subcontractors), the place of supply of those services in Spain will be Spain as the services are physically performed in Spain and taxable at 21%; the SL must register for Spanish VAT and may recover input VAT on related costs. However, warranty services supplied as part of an exported machinery contract may be treated as ancillary to the export and zero-rated if they are closely linked and satisfying the conditions of article 22 of the Spanish VAT Law.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.supply_chain_and_fiscal_representative_r: A non-resident exporter selling to Spanish customers on DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) or similar Incoterms where goods are physically imported into Spain from a third country is generally not the importer of record; the Spanish customer or an appointed customs agent acts as importer and pays import VAT (which may be deferred under the Import VAT deferral regime). However, if the non-resident entity is the importer of record, Spanish import VAT is due at border; a VAT registration in Spain is then necessary to deduct input VAT. No mandatory fiscal representative is required for an EU-incorporated entity; for non-EU entities, a Spanish VAT representative (responsable solidario) is mandatory unless the entity is resident in a country with a mutual assistance agreement (the List of countries with mutual assistance agreements includes most OECD/e-commerce countries; the UK is included per Decision (EU) 2021/1773, but a representative may still be required in practice).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to exports of goods outside the European Union, as defined in Articles 21(5) and 22(1) of Spanish VAT Law (Ley 37/1992) and EU VAT Directive Article 146(1)(a). Conditions: (a) the goods must be physically dispatched or transported from Spain to a destination outside the EU; (b) the dispatcher (seller, buyer or a third party acting on their behalf) must demonstrate that the goods have left the EU within the statutory period; (c) proof of export must be kept as prescribed; (d) the supply must be to a person or customer (private or business), but commercial evidence of transport must tie the goods to the export. For exports made by the Spanish SL as exporter: zero rating applies when the supplier (or an subcontractor) transports the goods out of the EU territory. For exports arranged by the purchaser (non-resident) or foreign customer: the supply is also zero-rated if the seller obtains adequate proof of export (including customs export declaration) and the other conditions are met. Exports to EU countries (e.g., another EU member state) are taxed at 0% as intra-Community supplies only if the goods are transported to another Member State and the customer communicates a valid VAT ID; otherwise, the supply may be taxable at 21% in Spain (e.g., if customer is not a taxable person or lacks VAT registration) — distance sales threshold rules apply for consumer sales. Services ancillary to an export (e.g., installation of the machinery outside Spain, technical directors, training provided in the foreign country) can be zero-rated if performed outside the EU or qualify as directly linked to the export of goods (Article 21(18) of Spanish VAT Law). For trial runs or services performed partly in Spain, an apportionment may be required. For aseptic bottling line (ISIC 2825), export zero rating generally applies to the transfer of ownership and physical export of fully assembled machinery; if the machinery is assembled and tested in Spain before export, the sale and transportation must still be documented as a single export contract. The Spanish export relief under article 21(5) requires that within 3 months of the supply (or 6 months if certain conditions/proofs under the ECS) the goods must have left EU customs territory; for goods sent for processing or repair the special regime under articles 23-24 applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/Customs Declaration SN) duly validated and accepted by Spanish Customs (AEAT, Departamento de Aduanas) with the Movement Reference Number (MRN) from the Export Control System (ECS)

Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), or CMR (international road consignment note) evidencing that goods have been transported to a destination outside the EU (or from Spain to another EU state for intra-Community supplies)

Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank Transfer Evidence (Proof of Payment received from foreign customer; while not a strict legal requirement for zero rating, it is expected in audit and AML/KYC documentation)
Commercial Invoice (with Incoterms, export declaration references, and Ex Works/FOB/EXW/CIF values)
Packing List with marks/numbers matching customs declarations

Customs export confirmation (C2 attestation, e-Export 'salida', or customs stamp/digital validation from AEAT, where applicable; for exports to EU: intra-Community supply summary recapitulative statement and the customer's valid VAT ID confirmation (VIES validation))
Intrastat or Recapitulative Statement (for intra-EU relevant declarations), if applicable
Optional but strongly recommended: Insurance certificate, certificate of origin, EUR.1/ATA Carnet where benefits under preferential trade agreements are claimed
Declaración de Frecuencia (export summary declaration) and supporting transport documents such as truck driver's declaration carrier's signature
Reasoned proof of export for cases where the goods are exported by the foreign customer (e.g., signed statement of dispatch by the Spanish supplier combined with customer's transport contract)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spanish customs and tax authorities (AEAT) subject export zero-rating to rigorous audit with risk-based criteria. If the exporter fails to retain and provide required proof of export within the legally required term (generally 180 days from the date of the invoice or transaction for record-keeping, but for intra-Community supplies the deadline to obtain proof of transport is often immediate with a maximum of 3-6 months), the supply may be recharacterised as taxable in Spain at 21% VAT, giving rise to an assessment (liquidación provisional), late-payment interest (interés de demora), and penalties. Penalties under Spanish General Taxation Law (Ley 58/2003): (a) incorrect self-assessment or omission: penalty of 50% to 100% of the amount at stake (Article 191 LGT) when there is intent or negligence; (b) failure to issue an invoice or incorrect invoice: penalty from €300 to €20,000 depending on circumstances; fines for failure to submit the SII or Veri*Factu records can range from €150 to €6,000 per batch. For fraudulent zero-rating, criminal tax fraud (delito contra la Hacienda Pública) applies when the defrauded amount exceeds €120,000, leading to imprisonment (1-6 years), fines and a court-ordered surcharge. Clawback (regularización) of input VAT deducted on export purchases is enforced if the corresponding export is not validated; the exporter must repay any VAT credits claimed. The statutory audit window (prescription period) is 4 years, but for cases involving fraud, the limitation period may extend to 10 years (or the period associated with the existence of unreported assets). AEAT may invoke the anti-abuse and sham transaction provisions (Article 15 and 16 LGT) to disregard the export if the purported export documentation is insufficient, falsified, or the goods did not actually leave EU territory. For intra-Community supplies, the reverse charge mechanism in the destination state may be denied if the supplier does not verify the customer's valid VAT number and obtain correct recapitulative statement; penalty for failure to submit recapitulative statements: fine of 1% of the total amount, minimum €300 per declaration (or €150 per two declarations). Additionally, the 180-day deadline specifically applies to exports where the supplier (or buyer) must show proof of export; for goods exported under the 'Ex O' procedure, the MRN must be available within 90 days from export declaration or 150 days in cases of authorised economic operator (subject to EC rules; under the UCC, the proof of export must be furnished within the term set by the transit or export customs procedure, generally within 90 days; Spain has up to 6 months under national provisions). To minimise risk, the SL must retain a structured export file, including the DUA with MRN, transport documents, evidence of payment in conformity with the 180-day repatriation deadline, and any bank statements evidencing FX conversion and inward remittance, because AEAT cross-checks these records via the 'International Exchange of Information' and customs database.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and under the monetary policy authority of the European Central Bank (ECB) pursuant to Article 127 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; foreign exchange administration is coordinated with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is a fully convertible free currency; Spain has no residual exchange-control restrictions from the pre-1992 regime. Current-account and capital-account transactions are equally liberalised under Article 63 TFEU and the ex-post FDI declaration framework of Law 19/2003. No prior administrative authorisation is required for dividend remittances, loan repayments, or capital repatriation for ISIC 2825 aseptic bottling line manufacturers, which sit outside the EU FDI screening categories of Regulation (EU) 2019/452. Profit remittance hurdles are purely administrative: (i) the Non-Resident Income Tax withholding framework (Royal Legislative Decree 5/2004) imposes a 19% withholding on treaty-protected third-country parents unless reduced by treaty (typically 5-10%), while EU/EEA parents benefit from zero withholding under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU); (ii) form 213/230 quarterly remittance slips must accompany each dividend payment to the tax office; (iii) a compliant SEPA or SWIFT MT103 payment instruction with an accurate purpose code must pass the bank's AML office. No convertibility ceiling or capital flow balancing mechanism applies to EUR-denominated intra-EU flows, and the Spanish Ministry does not apply exchange-rate approval gates for profit repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Spain abolished export-proceeds surrender and mandatory conversion obligations upon Euro adoption. Article 4 of Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 and Banco de España Balance-of-Payments statistical reporting (Circular 4/2019) impose no statutory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio: export collections in USD, CNY, or MXN may be retained freely in any Spanish or EU-resident account in the original currency. The only statutory burdens are: (i) monthly or quarterly Balance-of-Payments statistical reporting when aggregate export operations exceed EUR 1,000,000 per calendar year; (ii) the standard customs DUA (declaración única administrativa) at export; (iii) for discounted export credit ('pack credit' with recourse), documentary evidence at maturity (bill of lading and customs DUA) as the sole remittance-control support. There is no obligation to convert export proceeds into EUR or to hold them with any specific institution.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (EUR and foreign-currency operating accounts, escrow and collateral structures)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.notes: Largest domestic balance sheet; dedicated Trade and Transactional Banking desk for export automation; full SEPA, SWIFT MT103, LC, and dealing-room coverage for Latin American corridors.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BBVA - Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (capable of supporting capital-escrow structures)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.notes: Strong corporate FX hedging platform; digital onboarding with video-KYC for low-risk manufacturing profiles; Mexican and Latin American network suited for outbound sales of the aseptic bottling line.

Dense Spanish branch network and strongest SME export franchise; SME trade finance including LC discounting and ECA support; simple account documentation for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada structures.
Mid-corporate trade desk capable of competitive LC discounting; less extensive automated FX dealing platform; suitable as a secondary bank for treasury diversification.
Specialised in export-oriented mid-caps; leaner network and stricter onboarding for non-EU shareholders; may require higher compensating balances.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-LOW with strictly bounded utility. Spanish Electronic Money Institutions (entidades de dinero electrónico) and Payment Institutions must be authorised and supervised by Banco de España under Law 21/2011 (E-Money), PSD2, and Royal Decree-Law 19/2018. A non-European offshore EMI (Switzerland, United Kingdom, United States, Singapore, or Latin America) cannot lawfully hold resident SL treasury funds or clear EUR payments unless it maintains a fully passported EU authorisation; post-Brexit UK e-money institutions have lost passporting rights into Spain and are confined to an agent-entity model under Article 25 RDL 19/2018, registered in Banco de España's Special Register and subject to Circular 3/2023. Practical guidance: an offshore EMI account such as Wise Business, Airwallex, or a Swiss B-finance arm may be used only as a supplementary disbursement rail for low-value invoices, never as the primary treasury jurisdiction, and never where the SL must evidence a Spanish bank account to the Tax Agency (AEAT), a notary, or the Registro Mercantil. All idle treasury liquidity must remain in a Tier-1 licensed Spanish bank account for access to deposit-guarantee coverage under Directive 2014/49/EU (EUR 100,000) and for full audit transparency.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory at initial onboarding for non-resident directors and for ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of non-resident corporate shareholders under Spanish AML implementation (Law 10/2010), Banco de España Circular 3/2023, and SEPBLAC guidance. Standard practice requires a face-to-face interview (entrevista presencial) with the incorporating director and each beneficial owner, plus originals or notarised copies of passports and apostilled incorporation documents. Remote onboarding with video-identification is available only for EU/EEA passport holders having a Spanish NIE and where the corporate profile is rated standard low risk; a mixed team of Latin American or Asian shareholders must programme a physical branch visit to Madrid or Barcelona, or execute a public deed power-of-attorney before a Spanish notary or consulate with the Hague Apostille and a sworn translation into Spanish. Recommended mitigation architecture: appoint one Spanish-resident natural person as administrador único holding a local NIE, who executes the EIV (appointment of tax and AEAT representative), activates the corporate digital certificate (DNie or viafirma), and completes all KYC interviews on behalf of the non-resident owners, while each UBO provides a notarised power of attorney authenticated by the Hague Apostille.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO tax residency in a non-EU or high-risk jurisdiction (e.g., Panama, BVI, UAE, or a Latin American offshore trust structure).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation and register of beneficial owners (Registro de Titularidades Reales) of each corporate layer; consolidated group organogram; three years of audited financial statements of the shareholder; notarised passport copies and NIE of the Spanish resident administrator; sworn source-of-funds declaration supported by 12 months of bank statements originating from licensed banks only; ISIC 2825 and NAICS 333241 categorisation letter confirming low-risk aseptic packaging machinery manufacturing; signed EIV appointment of a local AML representative under Article 17 RDL 19/2018.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection to be wired from a non-bank money services business (e-money institution, crypto-fiat on-ramp, or FX broker) rather than a licensed credit institution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised escritura de aumento de capital; minutes of the shareholders' meeting (acta); certificate of the new paid-in capital issued by the Registro Mercantil within six months; bank confirmation that the origin account belongs to a licensed credit institution; sworn affidavit confirming that no cryptocurrency exchange or P2P platform was used; the underlying commercial agreement or sales contract justifying the transaction; Balance-of-Payments declaration template (D-1A) countersigned by an external auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected wire pattern mismatch: the company registers as a machinery manufacturer (ISIC 2825) but the transaction flow shows high-volume, low-value disbursements to Asian component suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed cash-flow forecast and procurement plan for the aseptic bottling line; concluded international supply agreements with Chinese or Taiwanese component vendors incorporating Incoterms 2020; customs broker appointment and EORI number authorisation; invoice-aging schedule for staged goods receipt; annual business plan endorsed by a Spanish registered auditor; formal request for a low-risk profile rating waiver submitted to the bank's AML compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or enhanced-screening hit triggered by maritime logistics counterparties, freight forwarders, or end-users located in or touching embargoed jurisdictions in the food-and-beverage export corridor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full OSINT sanctions screening report covering EU Regulation 269/2014, EU Regulation 833/2014, OFAC, and UK OFSI lists for all vessels, forwarders, and consignees; carrier and freight-forwarder compliance attestation letters; end-use certificate declaring civilian aseptic beverage bottling application only; complete set of L/C documents (bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin) naming the ultimate consignee; annual external legal opinion confirming absence of dual-use (military) applicability for HS 8422 and 8438 components; voluntary disclosure record to SEPBLAC in case of any near-miss event.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Recommended routing: SWIFT MT103 (serial cover) from the parent's Tier-1 correspondent bank, or a SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) where the parent maintains an EU euro account. Both rails preserve full remittance transparency. The payment instruction must carry the SEPA purpose code NESG (equity investment) in field 70 (Remittance Information), with free text 'AUMENTO DE CAPITAL - SOCIEDAD DE RESPONSABILIDAD LIMITADA' and the deed reference number in the Registro Mercantil. For non-EUR injections (e.g., USD from a Latin American parent), use SWIFT MT103 with the instruction 'RISK: DO NOT CONVERT' to prevent unauthorised off-market currency conversion at the beneficiary branch. Compliance verification prior to value date: (i) file the ex-post foreign direct investment declaration with the Investment Registry of the Ministry of Economy under Law 19/2003 (mandatory from EUR 9,000 per calendar year; no prior authorisation applies to ISIC 2825); (ii) run sanctions and PEP screening on the parent entity and its ultimate beneficial owners; (iii) deliver the notarial share-capital increase deed, acta, solvency balance, and certificación negativa from the Registro Mercantil for the bank's first-inbound-credit KYC review; (iv) submit a source-of-funds statement when the credit is USD-denominated and arrives via a correspondent outside the EEA.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary disbursement rails for the aseptic bottling line supply chain: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct TT-Wire to Western European machinery vendors in EUR, settled via TARGET2 with same-day finality and no FX cost; (ii) SWIFT MT202 COV for institution-to-institution cover payments when the beneficiary bank is outside the SEPA area; (iii) documentary Letters of Credit under UCP 600 (SWIFT MT700) as the standard instrument for exports to Latin American buyers (Mexico, Chile, Colombia) and for imports from Asian equipment manufacturers; (iv) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst, up to EUR 100,000) for urgent spare-part settlements; (v) USD-denominated commercial LC negotiation and discounting at Banco Santander or BBVA trade desks where the underlying contract invoices in USD. Trade documentation add-ons: banks verify bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, and destination-country sanitisation certificates before honouring each L/C. For spot conversion on USD or CNY disbursements, the corporate instructs the dealing room to transact at the published ECB reference rate plus 15-25 pips margin and must receive a pre-transaction benefit-rate confirmation under MiFID II disclosure rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/MXN) with maturities up to 24 months documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
FX swaps (principal exchange at both legs) for working-capital rollover and interbank treasury management
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) aligning USD-denominated capital expenditure debt with EUR-denominated revenue
Vanilla FX call and put options purchased for premium-only downside protection, with no speculative writing permitted for a non-financial counterparty

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on offshore CNY (USD/CNH) or restricted-convertibility Latin American currencies (USD/ARS, USD/COP), limited to a maximum 12-month tenor and executed only against a documented commercial trade flow
Embedded currency conversion clauses in export letters of credit under UCP 600 as a natural hedge mechanism

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved within six months after the financial year-end; filing must be completed within one month after approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in Registry closure and an administrative fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, or up to EUR 300,000 for entities with turnover exceeding EUR 6 million. Spain has no automatic annual administrative strike-off solely for late accounts filing; prolonged non-compliance may lead to dissolution or registry cancellation procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual accounts filing and updated whenever beneficial ownership changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate beneficial ownership information may prevent valid filing, cause Registry closure, and trigger administrative sanctions under Spanish anti-money-laundering legislation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year taxpayer, normally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties generally apply under the General Tax Law, with interest and potential surcharges; unpaid or underpaid tax may also generate tax penalties and enforcement proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary information return (Modelo 390), where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed during the first 30 calendar days of January following the reporting year, unless the taxpayer is exempt from filing due to its periodic VAT reporting profile.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, omitted, or incorrect filing may incur fixed or proportional tax penalties, depending on the applicable reporting obligation and the resulting tax impact.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder meeting and corporate resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; notarization and Mercantile Registry filing where legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary annual meeting must be held within six months after the end of the financial year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting may create director liability, impair approval and filing of accounts, and contribute to Registry closure or corporate governance disputes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Intrastat annual statistical reporting, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency and competent statistical reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly rather than annual reporting applies when EU goods movement thresholds and filing conditions are met; no filing is required below the applicable thresholds.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit required statistical declarations or submission of inaccurate information may result in administrative statistical penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is generally mandatory if, for two consecutive financial years, the company meets at least two of these three criteria: total assets exceeding EUR 2.85 million, net annual turnover exceeding EUR 5.7 million, or average employees exceeding 50. Mandatory audit also applies to certain regulated, public-interest, consolidated, or otherwise specially regulated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish accounting legislation. IFRS is generally not mandatory for an unlisted Spanish SL, except where a specific statutory or group-reporting requirement applies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain accurate beneficial ownership information and update it promptly after any change in ownership or control. The annual accounts filing includes a beneficial ownership declaration. Any share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members, supported by the relevant transfer documentation, and reflected in the beneficial ownership information where control changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Sole Shareholder, if applicable
Register of Directors and Attorneys-in-Fact, where applicable
Annual accounts and approved financial statements
Beneficial ownership records and supporting identification documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 400-1,500 per year, approximately USD 430-1,620, excluding extraordinary filings, notarization, courier, and document legalization costs.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 2,000-10,000 per year, approximately USD 2,160-10,800, depending on turnover, assets, transaction volume, inventory complexity, and audit scope.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created SL (first 2 tax periods with positive taxable base, subject to job and activity conditions); 25% standard; deductions for R&D (42% additional) and export activities; NOL carryforward unlimited (offset cap 70% for turnover <€20M; 50% for turnover ≥€20M)
